# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

## Scope

- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 89
  public definitions have no rows of their own: 85 (for example `kappa`,
  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,

     3	## The paper's argument and where Lean enters
     4	
     5	The paper bounds and identifies the growth of `log E[u(t,x)²]` for the
     6	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model. The argument has three layers.
     7	
     8	1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
     9	   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
    10	   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
    11	   imported bounds,
    12	   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
    13	   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
    14	   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
    15	   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
    16	   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
    17	   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
    18	   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
    19	   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
    20	   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
    21	   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
    22	   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
    23	   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
    24	   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
    25	   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
    26	   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
    27	   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
    28	   static controls
    29	   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
    30	   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
    31	   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
    32	   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
    33	   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
    34	   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
    35	   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
    36	   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
    37	   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
    38	   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
    39	   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
    40	   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
    41	   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
    42	   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
    43	   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
    44	   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
    45	   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
    46	   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
    47	   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
    48	   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
    49	   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
    50	   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
    51	   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
    52	   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
    53	   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
    54	   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
    55	   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
    56	   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
    57	   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
    58	   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
    59	   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
    60	   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
    61	   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
    62	   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
    63	2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
    64	   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
    65	   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
    66	   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
    67	   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
    68	   **These are what Lean checks.**
    69	3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**
    70	
    71	So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
    72	facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
    73	integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
    74	paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

   104	...": facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; the
   105	`StratonovichHAMAudit` step modules are all of this kind.
   106	
   107	Modules are counted by their ledger heading; a module that also proves
   108	pieces of other results is counted once. Completion modules
   109	(`ClockCopyHomog`, `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, `L9Completed`,
   110	`SpatialOccupationCompleted`, `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`,
   111	`IntervalScalarCompleted`, `L8Completed`) discharge named inputs of other
   112	modules; discharging an input does not make a narrower result whole, so
   113	`L8Completed` (narrower results, including `L:uniform-series-tail` with the
   114	chain measures fixed only by their masses) and the spatial and occupation
   115	modules remain "narrower result". `ClockCopyHomog`,
   116	`MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted` and `TimeSchur`, which have no section of
   117	their own, count as whole-result modules; `DampedNorms`, `SpectralHomog`,
   118	`TimeFractional`, `WaveKernel`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest` and
   119	`WeakSobolev` as foundations.
   120	
   121	These counts describe the package. They are not a percentage of the paper.
   122	The 28 whole results and 18 narrower results are deterministic lemmas,
   123	propositions and corollaries used inside the analytic argument, and the
   124	occupation ceiling `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (a narrower result: both
   125	forms with the exact constant, for `S_c^pos`; `C_2 <= U_2` not formalized);
   126	the other three main theorems are not formalized.
   127	
   128	## Reading a statement
   129	
   130	For each declaration, check three things against the paper:
   131	
   132	1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
   133	2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
   134	3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   135	   order agree.
   136	
   137	The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
   138	`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
   139	read without opening an editor.
   140	
   141	## Not yet included
   142	
   143	Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
   144	public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
   145	colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
   146	and will be added here when that library is released.

  225| \begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
  226|   Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
  227|   nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
  228|   $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
  229|   convention
  230|   \[
  231|     \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
  232|     \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
  233|   \]
  234|   The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
  235|   when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
  236|   $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
  237|   \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
  238|     \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
  239|   \end{equation}
  240|   with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
  241|   includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
  242| \end{hypothesis}

  803| \begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
  804|   \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
  805|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
  806|   in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
  807|   $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
  808|   \[
  809|     N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
  810|     N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
  811|     N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
  812|     \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
  813|   \]
  814|   Let
  815|   \[
  816|     K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
  817|     \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
  818|   \]
  819|   Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
  820|   $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
  821|   $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
  822|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
  823|     N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
  824|     N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
  825|   \end{equation}
  826|   More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
  827|   $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
  828|   by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
  829|   $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
  830|   and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
  831|   \[
  832|     K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
  833|     \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
  834|   \]
  835|   Then, for every $\theta>0$,
  836|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
  837|     \begin{split}
  838|       0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
  839|       0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
  840|     \end{split}
  841|   \end{equation}
  842|   These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
  843|   domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
  844|   scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
  845|   Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
  846|   give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
  847|   unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.
  848| \end{lemma}

 2531| \begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
 2532|   Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
 2533|   Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
 2534|   Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
 2535|   \[
 2536|     J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
 2537|   \]
 2538|   where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
 2539|   bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
 2540|   and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
 2541|   and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
 2542|   every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
 2543|   \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
 2544|     \begin{split}
 2545|       &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
 2546|       (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
 2547|       &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
 2548|       J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
 2549|     \end{split}
 2550|   \end{equation}
 2551|   The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
 2552|   whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
 2553| \end{lemma}

  142|   Let $T > 0$. The form
  143|   \[

  145|     = \int_0^T\int_0^T f(t)g(s)|t-s|^{-a}\ud t\ud s

   98| \begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
   99|   \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
  100|   On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
  101|   $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
  102|   h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
  103|   positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
  104|   \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
  105|     \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
  106|     =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
  107|     \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
  108|   \end{equation}
  109|   It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
  110|   positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
  111| \end{proposition}

   229	  \end{equation}
   230	  is a bijection of $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$, with inverse $D_{1/r}$. With
   231	  the same original covariance,
   232	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-dilation-values}
   233	    h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x)=r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx),\qquad
   234	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi,\qquad
   235	    \lambda_{D_r\Psi,s}=r\lambda_{\Psi,s},\quad
   236	    I_{D_r\Psi}=rI_\Psi.
   237	  \end{equation}
   238	\end{lemma}
   239	
   240	\begin{proof}
   241	  Positive dilation preserves the full smooth positive nonzero class;
   242	  multiplication of its amplitude powers gives the stated inverse. Homogeneity
   243	  of the physical Radon measure gives, for every nonnegative measurable $G$,
   244	  \[
   245	    \int G(ry)\Gamma(\ud y)
   246	    =r^{\alpha-d}\int G(z)\Gamma(\ud z).
   247	  \]
   248	  Indeed, its left pushforward measure on a Borel set $A$ is $\Gamma(A/r) =
   249	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$. Positive Tonelli applies this identity inside the
   250	  temporal convolution, giving $h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x) = r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx)$. Now use
   251	  the \emph{Lebesgue} substitution $z = rx$ in the original pairing:
   252	  \[
   253	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{d+2-\alpha}r^2r^{-d}v_\Psi
   254	    =r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi.
   255	  \]
   256	  This distinguishes the Radon pushforward from the spatial volume factor; it
   257	  includes singular covariances and white noise.
   258	
   259	  The map $U_rf(x) = r^{d/2}f(rx)$ is a unitary bijection on real $L^2$,
   260	  preserving $H^1,H^2$ as sets under its inverse. Weak derivatives give
   261	  $\|\nabla U_rf\|_2^2 = r^2\|\nabla f\|_2^2$ and $\int h_{D_r\Psi,s}(U_rf)^2 =
   262	  r^2\int h_{\Psi,s}f^2$. The real Rayleigh bijection proves the squared rate
   263	  identity; the rates are positive, so their square roots and integrals give
   264	  \eqref{E:variational-dilation-values}. On $H^2$ this is also $H_{D_r\Psi,s}U_r
   265	  = r^2U_rH_{\Psi,s}$. Time has not been rescaled. For compact masks the
   266	  corresponding identity uses $m_R(rx) = m_{R/r}(x)$; a fixed mask radius is not
   267	  invariant. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation}.
   268	\end{proof}
## VariationalDilation (narrower result: `L:variational-control-dilation`, rate and variance identification not formalized)

Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-control-dilation` (Radon and Rayleigh
dilation; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines 225-268 at
`a284420`) together with the definitions it uses, in two modules:
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WeakSobolev.lean` (a hand-built real Sobolev
space and the real Rayleigh value set) and
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalDilation.lean` (the control class,
the dilation, the mean, variance, rate and integrated rate, and the lemma).
The wrapper `variational_control_dilation_paper` states the lemma with the
section's standing hypotheses (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying
`H:homog`, modelled by `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`, with `a = alpha0`):
for `r > 0`, `D_r` is a bijection of the class with inverse `D_(1/r)`, and the
four identities of `E:variational-dilation-values` hold. Nothing is supplied as
a hypothesis.

Abstractions and why they are faithful.
The class `E:variational-positive-class` (lines 5-10) consists of smooth
functions on `R x R^d` with compact support inside `(0,1) x R^d`, i.e. elements
of `C_c^infinity((0,1) x R^d)` extended by zero. `CPos_nonempty` proves that
the class is nonempty (lines 13-17) using a different bump. The mean
`h_{Psi,s}` and the variance `v_Psi` are the
displays `E:compact-raw-mean` and `E:compact-raw-cost`
(`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex` lines 402-412), with
`(Gamma * phi)(x) = int phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)` and `int_0^1` taken over
`Ioo 0 1`. Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces, so `WeakSobolev` defines
`H^1(R^d; R)` by weak gradients (`int f d_v phi = -int <g,v> phi` for every
test function `phi` and direction `v`). It proves that an `L^2` weak gradient
- `Psi` is continuous; this follows from smoothness.
- The identities hold for every real `s`, not only for `s in [0,1]`.

Junk values. Every identity is an exact identity of Bochner integrals and of
`sSup`. It would remain true if an integrand were not integrable, or if the
Rayleigh set were empty or unbounded (Lean's value `0` on both sides). The
companion does not exclude these junk cases. It proves only conditional
transfers, in `variational_control_dilation_integrable_paper`:
- every integrand in the definitions of `h`, `v` and `I` is integrable for
  `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`;
- the Rayleigh sets themselves scale, so a Rayleigh set is nonempty and
  bounded above for `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`.

So if a quantity is a genuine integral or supremum for `Psi`, the identity
relates it to a genuine integral or supremum for `D_r Psi`. For
`s in [0,1]`, `VariationalMean` proves that the integrand of `h_s(x)` is
integrable and that `h_s` is bounded (`L:variational-global-mean`,
`variational_global_mean_paper`), so the mean identity relates genuine
integrals there. That the variance and rate integrands are integrable, and
that the Rayleigh sets are nonempty and bounded above, is not proved in
this module. For `Psi in C_pos` under the section's hypotheses these are
proved in `VariationalRate` (`rawCost_genuine`, `unmasked_rate`); the
identifications `v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2` and `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)` remain
outside Lean. The
integrability equivalences are Lean-route auxiliaries: the TeX proof
(lines 243-250) works with nonnegative integrands and Tonelli and states none
of them. Their rows below say so.

The TeX's square-root step uses positivity of the rates. Lean instead uses
`sqrt(sSup(r^2 S)) = r sqrt(sSup S)`, which holds for every set `S`.

Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0`, and every clause of `H:homog`
except the set scaling. The general theorems assume only the set scaling
`SetScaling` and continuity of `Psi`.

   339	  \label{L:raw-block-restart}
   340	  Fix $\delta,B,N$ and let $L = \delta^{-1}$, $L_{\mathrm{ext}} = (N+1)B \ge L$.
   341	  On this global fast horizon define $A_{\mathrm{glob}} = g_\delta
   342	  A_R(W_{\mathrm{fast}})$. Its physical flow obeys
   343	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-restart}
   344	    P_{\mathrm{glob}}(mB+u,mB)=D_m^0(u),\qquad 0\le u\le B.
   345	  \end{equation}
   346	  The analogous identity holds with the deterministic mean $V_{\delta t}$ added
   347	  globally and local operator paths $X_m+H_m$. Their finite block products,
   348	  including the last remainder $\tau$, are source limits in $L^2$, at this fixed
   349	  $\delta,N$.
   350	\end{lemma}

   353	  Take one regularized slow noise preserving the given noise $Y_{\epsilon,\eta}$
   354	  on the extension of the given $W$ constructed in
   355	  Section~\ref{S:source-driver-convergence}. Define the fast and local noises by

   358	    Y_m(f)=Y_{\epsilon,\eta}(T_{\delta,m}f).
   359	  \]

   361	  residual variance bounds by $\|f\|_{H_W}^2$. The residual tends to zero on

   363	  retained. Proposition~\ref{P:source-gaussian-transfer} therefore gives the

   149	\begin{lemma}[Real Gram realization]\label{L:gram-realization}
   150	  Every finite real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix is the Gram matrix of
   151	  vectors in a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space. When its entries are
   152	  nonnegative, the value $\mathscr{S}(C)$ is independent of its realization.
   153	\end{lemma}
   154	
   155	\begin{proof}
   156	  Induct on the size, with the empty matrix realized in $\{0\}$. Diagonal
   157	  entries are nonnegative. If all vanish, testing on $e_i+t e_j$ gives $2tC_{ij}
   158	  \ge 0$ for every real $t$, hence $C = 0$, realized by zero vectors. Otherwise
   159	  permute a positive diagonal $c$ into the first position and write $C =
   160	  \left[\begin{smallmatrix}c&v^{\mathsf{T}}\\v&A\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. The
   161	  Schur complement $B = A-vv^{\mathsf{T}}/c$ is positive semidefinite: test the
   162	  original quadratic form on $(-v^{\mathsf{T}}y/c,y)$. Realize $B$ by vectors
   163	  $u_i$ using the induction hypothesis. Then $k_1 = (\sqrt c,0)$ and $k_i =
   164	  (v_i/\sqrt c,u_i)$ for the other indices realize $C$. Undo the permutation.
   165	  Entries of $B$ need not be nonnegative; this construction requires neither
   166	  nonnegative coordinates nor complete positivity.
   167	
   168	  In any realization, $C_{ii} = 0$ means $k_i = 0$, so its entire row vanishes.
   169	  Formula~\eqref{E:gram-active-duality} depends only on $C,\ell,b$ and these
   170	  eligible indices. It therefore proves realization independence whenever the
   171	  entries are nonnegative, which is the scope in which $\mathscr{S}(C)$ is used.
   172	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:gram-realization}.
   173	\end{proof}

   175	\begin{proposition}[Entrywise Gram comparison]\label{P:gram-entrywise-comparison}
   176	  Let $C,D$ be real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices on the same finite
   177	  index set, with $0 \le C_{ij} \le D_{ij}$. With the same $\ell_i > 0,b_i \ge
   178	  0$,
   179	  \[
   180	    \mathscr{S}(C)\le\mathscr{S}(D).
   181	  \]
   182	  No positive-semidefinite order on $D-C$ is required.
   183	\end{proposition}
   184	
   185	\begin{proof}
   186	  Lemma~\ref{L:gram-realization} defines both values. Their eligible sets
   187	  satisfy $\mathcal{J}_C \subset \mathcal{J}_D$. For nonempty $A \subset
   188	  \mathcal{J}_C$ and positive weights,
   189	  \[
   190	    D_A^D(w)-D_A^C(w)

   194	  maxima and using the inclusion of eligible families proves the claim by
   195	  Proposition~\ref{P:gram-positive-optimizer}. This includes the appearance of
   196	  previously zero vectors. This proves
   197	  Proposition~\ref{P:gram-entrywise-comparison}.
   198	\end{proof}
